info.label: Vertigo
info.desc: Brothers in Arms is the fifth studio album by British rock band Dire Straits, released in 1985. The first half of the album is a development of their unique brand of arena rock which had evolved in their music since the 1980 album Making Movies, while the second half consists of more folk-influenced material. The whole album maintains the original Dire Straits' bluesy and laid back guitar-based sound whilst retaining a more lavish and bombastic production and overall sound. It is the band's best selling album. Brothers in Arms was one of the first albums to be directed at the .
info.engineers: Steve Jackson (2), Bruce Lampcov, Dave Greenberg, Neil Dorfsman / Bob Ludwig, John Dent

podcast.body: Dire Straits' "Brothers in Arms" was the first Compact Disc to sell more than one million copies, achieving this milestone in 1985. This represented a significant commercial success for the relatively new CD format and for the band. "The first compact disc to sell more than a million copies was Brothers and Arms by Dyer Straits that happened in 1985."

podcast.body: Dire Straits' *Brothers in Arms* album, released in 1985, became the first million-seller CD. This achievement demonstrated the commercial viability and growing popularity of the compact disc format, dispelling initial industry skepticism. "And the first artist to have a million seller CD was Dyer Straits with their Brothers in Arms album in 1985."

podcast.body: Released in 1985, *Brothers in Arms* is widely recognized as the first AAD album. The recording process was analog, but the mastering and mixing were done digitally, and the physical format was digital. Its status as the "first" is controversial due to the progressive integration of digital effects into many analog recordings, blurring the exact line of transition. "Llegamos a 1985 cuando sale Brothers In Hals de Dades Trades, que se considera el primer disco a de... se grabó en analógico, pero el proceso de masterización y mezclado ya era digital y se hacían formatos digitales el formato físico."

srcs.episode: El cambio de Musica analogica a musica digital.

podcast.body: This album, Dire Straits' fifth studio effort, was recorded at Air Studios on the island of Montserrat. It became a global number one smash, topping charts around the world, including in America, and sold more than 30 million copies. It featured guest harmony vocals from Sting on the track "Money for Nothing." "Money for Nothing and the Brothers in Arms LP wound up topping charts around the world, including in America, and sold more than 30 million copies."

srcs.episode: If You Love Sting, Set Him Free Edition Part 2

podcast.body: This album, noted for its beautiful recording, became the first compact disc to sell a million copies by 1986. Philips, a key developer of CD technology, sponsored Dire Straits' tour in support of this digitally recorded album, with leader Mark Knopfler appearing in a TV commercial extolling the CD's virtues. "Dire Straits, Brothers and Arms album, a beautifully recorded album, became the first CD to sell a million copies."
